sanskrit: pariśrāntaṃ gataṃ bhūmau kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram tavāntevāsinaṃ śūraṃ pālayārjuna sātyakim
english: "Worn out and brought to the ground, after performing a deed most hard to do, is your own pupil, the brave Sātyaki. Protect him, Arjuna!"

sanskrit: na vaśaṃ yajñaśīlasya gacched eṣa varārihan tvatkṛte puruṣavyāghra tad āśu kriyatāṃ vibho
english: "Let him not fall into the power of this lover of sacrifices, O best slayer of foes. For your own sake, O tiger among men, let it be done at once, O mighty one!"

sanskrit: athābravīd dhṛṣṭamanā vāsudevaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ paśya vṛṣṇipravīreṇa krīḍantaṃ kurupuṃgavam mahādvipeneva vane mattena hariyūthapam
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, his mind exultant, said to Vāsudeva: "Look at that bull of the Kurus sporting with the foremost hero of the Vṛṣṇis—as a furious great elephant in the forest sports with the leader of a lion-pride."

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīt sainyānāṃ bharatarṣabha yad udyamya mahābāhuḥ sātyakiṃ nyahanad bhuvi
english: A great cry of dismay went up from the armies, O bull of the Bharatas, when the mighty-armed one, lifting Sātyaki up, struck him down to the ground.

sanskrit: sa siṃha iva mātaṅgaṃ vikarṣan bhūridakṣiṇaḥ vyarocata kuruśreṣṭhaḥ sātvatapravaraṃ yudhi
english: Dragging the foremost of the Sātvatas like a lion hauling an elephant, the best of the Kurus, lavish in his sacrificial gifts, shone resplendent in the battle.

sanskrit: atha kośād viniṣkṛṣya khaḍgaṃ bhūriśravā raṇe mūrdhajeṣu nijagrāha padā corasy atāḍayat
english: Then, drawing his sword from its sheath in the fray, Bhūriśravas seized Sātyaki by the hair and struck him on the chest with his foot.

sanskrit: tathā tu parikṛṣyantaṃ dṛṣṭvā sātvatam āhave vāsudevas tato rājan bhūyo 'rjunam abhāṣata
english: Seeing the Sātvata thus being dragged about in the battle, O king, Vāsudeva spoke once more to Arjuna:

sanskrit: paśya vṛṣṇyandhakavyāghraṃ saumadattivaśaṃ gatam tava śiṣyaṃ mahābāho dhanuṣy anavaraṃ tvayā
english: "Behold this tiger of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas fallen into the power of Somadatta's son—your own pupil, O mighty-armed one, second to none but you in archery!"

sanskrit: asatyo vikramaḥ pārtha yatra bhūriśravā raṇe viśeṣayati vārṣṇeyaṃ sātyakiṃ satyavikramam
english: "Untrue is the show of valor, O Pārtha, when in this battle Bhūriśravas gets the better of Sātyaki of the Vṛṣṇis, whose own prowess is true."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahābāhur vāsudevena pāṇḍavaḥ manasā pūjayām āsa bhūriśravasam āhave
english: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, the mighty-armed son of Pāṇḍu honored Bhūriśravas in his heart for his conduct in the battle:

sanskrit: vikarṣan sātvataśreṣṭhaṃ krīḍamāna ivāhave saṃharṣayati māṃ bhūyaḥ kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ
english: "Dragging the foremost of the Sātvatas about, as if in sport in the battle, this enhancer of the Kurus' glory delights me all the more."

sanskrit: pravaraṃ vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ yan na hanyād dhi sātyakim mahādvipam ivāraṇye mṛgendra iva karṣati
english: "For he does not slay Sātyaki, the foremost of the Vṛṣṇi heroes; like a lion dragging a great elephant in the forest, so does he haul him about."

sanskrit: evaṃ tu manasā rājan pārthaḥ saṃpūjya kauravam vāsudevaṃ mahābāhur arjunaḥ pratyabhāṣata
english: Thus having honored the Kaurava in his heart, O king, the mighty-armed Pārtha, Arjuna, replied to Vāsudeva:

sanskrit: saindhavāsaktadṛṣṭitvān nainaṃ paśyāmi mādhava eṣa tv asukaraṃ karma yādavārthe karomy aham
english: "Since my gaze is fixed upon the lord of the Sindhus, I do not see him clearly, O Mādhava. Yet this hard deed I will do, for the Yādava's sake."

sanskrit: ity uktvā vacanaṃ kurvan vāsudevasya pāṇḍavaḥ sakhaḍgaṃ yajñaśīlasya patriṇā bāhum acchinat
english: So saying, and carrying out the word of Vāsudeva, the son of Pāṇḍu with a feathered shaft severed the sword-wielding arm of that lover of sacrifices.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa bāhur apatad bhūmau sakhaḍgaḥ saśubhāṅgadaḥ ādadhaj jīvalokasya duḥkham uttamam uttamaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: That noble arm, still gripping the sword and bright with its fair armlet, fell to the ground, bringing the keenest grief to the world of the living.

sanskrit: prahariṣyan hṛto bāhur adṛśyena kirīṭinā vegenābhyapatad bhūmau pañcāsya iva pannagaḥ
english: That arm, raised to strike but cut off by the unseen Kirīṭin, fell swiftly to the earth like a five-headed serpent.

sanskrit: sa moghaṃ kṛtam ātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthena kauravaḥ utsṛjya sātyakiṃ krodhād garhayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: Seeing himself thus thwarted by Pārtha, the Kaurava released Sātyaki and in his wrath rebuked the son of Pāṇḍu:

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaṃ bata kaunteya karmedaṃ kṛtavān asi apaśyato viṣaktasya yan me bāhum acicchidaḥ
english: "A cruel deed, alas, O son of Kuntī, you have done, in that you cut off my arm while I was looking elsewhere, my mind engaged with another."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyasi rājānaṃ dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram kiṃ kurvāṇo mayā saṃkhye hato bhūriśravā iti
english: "What will you say to King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma? 'Bhūriśravas was slain by me in battle while doing what?'"

sanskrit: idam indreṇa te sākṣād upadiṣṭaṃ mahātmanā astraṃ rudreṇa vā pārtha droṇenātha kṛpeṇa vā
english: "Was this the weapon taught you in person by great-souled Indra, O Pārtha, or by Rudra, or by Droṇa, or by Kṛpa?"

sanskrit: nanu nāma svadharmajñas tvaṃ loke 'bhyadhikaḥ paraiḥ ayudhyamānasya kathaṃ raṇe prahṛtavān asi
english: "Are you not indeed known throughout the world as one who knows his own duty, surpassing others? How then have you struck in battle a man not fighting against you?"

sanskrit: na pramattāya bhītāya virathāya prayācate vyasane vartamānāya praharanti manasvinaḥ
english: "Men of wisdom do not strike one who is heedless, one who is afraid, one whose chariot is gone, one who begs for mercy, or one caught in distress."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu nīcācaritam asatpuruṣasevitam katham ācaritaṃ pārtha tvayā karma suduṣkaram
english: "This base conduct, practiced only by ignoble men—how have you, O Pārtha, performed so unworthy a deed?"

sanskrit: āryeṇa sukaraṃ hy āhur āryakarma dhanaṃjaya anāryakarma tv āryeṇa suduṣkarataraṃ bhuvi
english: "For they say a noble deed is easy for a noble man, O Dhanaṃjaya; but an ignoble deed done by a noble man is the hardest thing on earth."

sanskrit: yeṣu yeṣu naraḥ pārtha yatra yatra ca vartate āśu tacchīlatām eti tad idaṃ tvayi dṛśyate
english: "In whatever company a man moves, O Pārtha, and in whatever circumstances he lives, he soon takes on its character—and this is seen now in you."

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi rājavaṃśyas tvaṃ kauraveyo viśeṣataḥ kṣatradharmād apakrāntaḥ suvṛttaś caritavrataḥ
english: "How is it that you, born of a royal line, and a Kaurava above all, of fair conduct and faithful to your vows, have strayed from the duty of a warrior?"

sanskrit: idaṃ tu yad atikṣudraṃ vārṣṇeyārthe kṛtaṃ tvayā vāsudevamataṃ nūnaṃ naitat tvayy upapadyate
english: "This utterly mean act, done by you for the Vṛṣṇi's sake, was surely the counsel of Vāsudeva—it does not befit you."

sanskrit: ko hi nāma pramattāya pareṇa saha yudhyate īdṛśaṃ vyasanaṃ dadyād yo na kṛṣṇasakho bhavet
english: "For who that was not the friend of Kṛṣṇa would inflict such a calamity upon a man engaged in fighting with another?"

sanskrit: vrātyāḥ saṃśliṣṭakarmāṇaḥ prakṛtyaiva vigarhitāḥ vṛṣṇyandhakāḥ kathaṃ pārtha pramāṇaṃ bhavatā kṛtāḥ
english: "The Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas are outcastes given to vile dealings, despised by their very nature—how, O Pārtha, have you made them your standard?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur yūpaketur mahāyaśāḥ yuyudhānaṃ parityajya raṇe prāyam upāviśat
english: Having said this, the mighty-armed and far-famed hero of the sacrificial-post banner abandoned Yuyudhāna and sat down upon the battlefield to fast unto death.

sanskrit: śarān āstīrya savyena pāṇinā puṇyalakṣaṇaḥ yiyāsur brahmalokāya prāṇān prāṇeṣv athājuhot
english: Spreading out arrows with his left hand, that man of holy marks, desiring to go to the world of Brahmā, then offered his life-breaths as an oblation into the breaths themselves.

sanskrit: sūrye cakṣuḥ samādhāya prasannaṃ salile manaḥ dhyāyan mahopaniṣadaṃ yogayukto 'bhavan muniḥ
english: Fixing his eyes upon the sun and his serene mind upon the waters, meditating on the great mystic doctrine and joined in yoga, he became a sage.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa sarvasenāyāṃ janaḥ kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau garhayām āsa taṃ cāpi śaśaṃsa puruṣarṣabham
english: Then throughout all the host the men reproached Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya, and they praised that bull among men.

sanskrit: nindyamānau tathā kṛṣṇau nocatuḥ kiṃ cid apriyam praśasyamānaś ca tathā nāhṛṣyad yūpaketanaḥ
english: Though thus reviled, the two Kṛṣṇas said nothing unkind in reply; and though thus praised, the bearer of the sacrificial-post banner felt no elation.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā vādino rājan putrāṃs tava dhanaṃjayaḥ amṛṣyamāṇo manasā teṣāṃ tasya ca bhāṣitam
english: O king, Dhanaṃjaya, unable in his heart to bear those words of your sons and of Bhūriśravas as they spoke,

sanskrit: asaṃkruddhamanā vācā smārayann iva bhārata uvāca pāṇḍutanayaḥ sākṣepam iva phalgunaḥ
english: yet with a mind free of anger, as if reminding them, O Bhārata, the son of Pāṇḍu, Phalguna, spoke, almost with a tone of reproach:

sanskrit: mama sarve 'pi rājāno jānanty etan mahāvratam na śakyo māmako hantuṃ yo me syād bāṇagocare
english: "All the kings know this great vow of mine: that none of my own people may be slain by another, if he comes within the range of my arrows."

sanskrit: yūpaketo samīkṣya tvaṃ na māṃ garhitum arhasi na hi dharmam avijñāya yuktaṃ garhayituṃ param
english: "O bearer of the sacrificial-post banner, reflect, and you ought not to censure me; for it is not right to blame another without first understanding the law."

sanskrit: āttaśastrasya hi raṇe vṛṣṇivīraṃ jighāṃsataḥ yad ahaṃ bāhum acchaitsaṃ na sa dharmo vigarhitaḥ
english: "That in battle I cut off the arm of you who, weapon in hand, were bent on slaying the Vṛṣṇi hero—that is no conduct to be condemned."

sanskrit: nyastaśastrasya bālasya virathasya vivarmaṇaḥ abhimanyor vadhaṃ tāta dhārmikaḥ ko na pūjayet
english: "As for the slaying of Abhimanyu—a mere boy, his weapons laid down, his chariot lost, his armor gone—what righteous man, dear sir, would commend it?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena śirasā bhūmim aspṛśat pāṇinā caiva savyena prāhiṇod asya dakṣiṇam
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, Bhūriśravas touched the ground with his head, and with his left hand he flung aside his own severed right arm.

sanskrit: etat pārthasya tu vacas tataḥ śrutvā mahādyutiḥ yūpaketur mahārāja tūṣṇīm āsīd avāṅmukhaḥ
english: Having heard these words of Pārtha, the splendid bearer of the sacrificial-post banner, O great king, fell silent, his face bowed down.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yā prītir dharmarāje me bhīme ca vadatāṃ vare nakule sahadeve ca sā me tvayi śalāgraja
english: Arjuna said: "The love I bear to the King of Righteousness, and to Bhīma, best of speakers, and to Nakula and Sahadeva—that same love I bear to you, O elder brother of Śala."

sanskrit: mayā tu samanujñātaḥ kṛṣṇena ca mahātmanā gaccha puṇyakṛtāṃl lokāñ śibir auśīnaro yathā
english: "With my leave, and that of great-souled Kṛṣṇa, go now to the worlds of those who have done holy deeds, even as Śibi, the son of Uśīnara, once did."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tata utthāya śaineyo vimuktaḥ saumadattinā khaḍgam ādāya cicchitsuḥ śiras tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the grandson of Śini, released by Somadatta's son, rose up and, taking up his sword, sought to cut off the head of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: nihataṃ pāṇḍuputreṇa pramattaṃ bhūridakṣiṇam iyeṣa sātyakir hantuṃ śalāgrajam akalmaṣam
english: Sātyaki sought to slay that sinless elder brother of Śala—the lavish giver of sacrificial gifts—who, while heedless, had already been struck down by the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: nikṛttabhujam āsīnaṃ chinnahastam iva dvipam krośatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ nindyamānaḥ sudurmanāḥ
english: As all the troops cried out, Sātyaki, reviled by them and sick at heart, advanced upon him as he sat with his arm hewn off, like an elephant whose trunk has been severed.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇaḥ sa kṛṣṇena pārthena ca mahātmanā bhīmena cakrarakṣābhyām aśvatthāmnā kṛpeṇa ca
english: Though restrained by Kṛṣṇa, by great-souled Pārtha, by Bhīma, by the two wheel-guards, by Aśvatthāman and by Kṛpa,

sanskrit: karṇena vṛṣasenena saindhavena tathaiva ca vikrośatāṃ ca sainyānām avadhīt taṃ yatavratam
english: and by Karṇa, by Vṛṣasena and by the lord of the Sindhus as well, and amid the outcry of all the troops, he slew that man of disciplined vows.

sanskrit: prāyopaviṣṭāya raṇe pārthena chinnabāhave sātyakiḥ kauravendrāya khaḍgenāpāharac chiraḥ
english: As that Kaurava lord, his arm cut off by Pārtha, sat fasting unto death on the battlefield, Sātyaki struck off his head with his sword.

sanskrit: nābhyanandanta tatsainyāḥ sātyakiṃ tena karmaṇā arjunena hataṃ pūrvaṃ yaj jaghāna kurūdvaham
english: The troops did not applaud Sātyaki for that deed—that he had slain this glory of the Kurus who had already been struck down before by Arjuna.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣasamaṃ tatra siddhacāraṇamānavāḥ bhūriśravasam ālokya yuddhe prāyagataṃ hatam
english: There the Siddhas, the Cāraṇas, and men alike, beholding Bhūriśravas—the equal of the thousand-eyed Indra—slain in battle as he sat fasting,

sanskrit: apūjayanta taṃ devā vismitās tasya karmabhiḥ pakṣavādāṃś ca bahuśaḥ prāvadaṃs tasya sainikāḥ
english: the gods honored him, amazed at his deeds; and his own soldiers spoke many words taking his part.

sanskrit: na vārṣṇeyasyāparādho bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā tasmān manyur na vaḥ kāryaḥ krodho duḥkhakaro nṛṇām
english: "It is no fault of the Vṛṣṇi, for what was destined had to be so. Therefore you should bear him no grudge—wrath only brings grief to men."

sanskrit: hantavyaś caiṣa vīreṇa nātra kāryā vicāraṇā vihito hy asya dhātraiva mṛtyuḥ sātyakir āhave
english: "This hero was fated to be slain, and on that there should be no debate; for the Ordainer himself had appointed Sātyaki to be his death in battle."

sanskrit: sātyakir uvāca na hantavyo na hantavya iti yan māṃ prabhāṣatha dharmavādair adharmiṣṭhā dharmakañcukam āsthitāḥ
english: Sātyaki said: "You who tell me, 'He must not be slain, he must not be slain,' with your talk of righteousness—most unrighteous men, you have wrapped yourselves in a mere cloak of righteousness!"

sanskrit: yadā bālaḥ subhadrāyāḥ sutaḥ śastravinākṛtaḥ yuṣmābhir nihato yuddhe tadā dharmaḥ kva vo gataḥ
english: "When the boy, Subhadrā's son, stripped of his weapons, was slain by you in battle—where then had your righteousness gone?"

sanskrit: mayā tv etat pratijñātaṃ kṣepe kasmiṃś cid eva hi yo māṃ niṣpiṣya saṃgrāme jīvan hanyāt padā ruṣā sa me vadhyo bhavec chatrur yady api syān munivrataḥ
english: "This vow I once made, upon some taunt or other: that whoever should crush me in battle and, while I yet lived, strike me with his foot in fury—that enemy should be slain by me, even were he bound by the vows of a sage."

sanskrit: ceṣṭamānaṃ pratīghāte sabhujaṃ māṃ sacakṣuṣaḥ manyadhvaṃ mṛtam ity evam etad vo buddhilāghavam yukto hy asya pratīghātaḥ kṛto me kurupuṃgavāḥ
english: "You, who have eyes, deem me dead though I was struggling to strike back and still had my arm—such is the shallowness of your judgment! The retaliation I have wrought upon him was fitting, O bulls of the Kurus."

sanskrit: yat tu pārthena matsnehāt svāṃ pratijñāṃ ca rakṣatā sakhaḍgo 'sya hṛto bāhur etenaivāsmi vañcitaḥ
english: "That Pārtha, out of love for me and to keep his own vow, cut off this man's sword-bearing arm—by that very act I have been cheated of my due."

sanskrit: bhavitavyaṃ ca yad bhāvi daivaṃ ceṣṭayatīva ca so 'yaṃ hato vimarde 'smin kim atrādharmaceṣṭitam
english: "What is to be must be, and fate, as it were, drives men to act. He has been slain in this fray—what unrighteous deed is there in that?"

sanskrit: api cāyaṃ purā gītaḥ śloko vālmīkinā bhuvi pīḍākaram amitrāṇāṃ yat syāt kartavyam eva tat
english: "And moreover this verse was sung of old by Vālmīki upon the earth: 'Whatever brings harm to one's enemies, that very thing must be done.'"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam ukte mahārāja sarve kauravapāṇḍavāḥ na sma kiṃ cid abhāṣanta manasā samapūjayan
english: Saṃjaya said: When this had been spoken, O great king, all the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas said nothing, but honored Bhūriśravas in their hearts.

sanskrit: mantrair hi pūtasya mahādhvareṣu; yaśasvino bhūrisahasradasya muner ivāraṇyagatasya tasya; na tatra kaś cid vadham abhyanandat
english: For of him—purified by sacred chants at his great rites, glorious, the giver of countless thousands, now like a sage gone to the forest—of his slaying not one there approved.

sanskrit: sunīlakeśaṃ varadasya tasya; śūrasya pārāvatalohitākṣam aśvasya medhyasya śiro nikṛttaṃ; nyastaṃ havirdhānam ivottareṇa
english: The head of that bounteous, brave one, dark-blue-haired and dove-red of eye, lay severed like the head of a sacrificial horse set down to the north of the oblation-cart.

sanskrit: sa tejasā śastrahatena pūto; mahāhave dehavaraṃ visṛjya ākrāmad ūrdhvaṃ varado varārho; vyāvṛtya dharmeṇa pareṇa rodasī
english: Purified by that splendor smitten down by the sword, he cast off his noble body in the great battle, and that bounteous one, worthy of the highest boons, rose upward, filling heaven and earth with his surpassing righteousness.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ajito droṇarādheyavikarṇakṛtavarmabhiḥ tīrṇaḥ sainyārṇavaṃ vīraḥ pratiśrutya yudhiṣṭhire
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Unconquered by Droṇa, by Rādheya, by Vikarṇa and Kṛtavarman, that hero, having pledged himself to Yudhiṣṭhira, had crossed the ocean of the army.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ kauraveyeṇa samareṣv anivāritaḥ nigṛhya bhūriśravasā balād bhuvi nipātitaḥ
english: How was it that he, unchecked in battle, came to be seized by the Kaurava Bhūriśravas and hurled by force to the ground?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājann ihotpattiṃ śaineyasya yathā purā yathā ca bhūriśravaso yatra te saṃśayo nṛpa
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, the origin of the grandson of Śini in days of old, and that of Bhūriśravas as well, wherein lies your doubt, O lord of men.

sanskrit: atreḥ putro 'bhavat somaḥ somasya tu budhaḥ smṛtaḥ budhasyāsīn mahendrābhaḥ putra ekaḥ purūravāḥ
english: From Atri was born Soma; of Soma, Budha is recorded; and Budha had one son, Purūravas, splendid as the great Indra.

sanskrit: purūravasa āyus tu āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ smṛtaḥ nahuṣasya yayātis tu rājarṣir devasaṃmitaḥ
english: Of Purūravas came Āyus; of Āyus, Nahuṣa is recorded; and of Nahuṣa, Yayāti, a royal sage held equal to the gods.

sanskrit: yayāter devayānyāṃ tu yadur jyeṣṭho 'bhavat sutaḥ yador abhūd anvavāye devamīḍha iti śrutaḥ
english: Of Yayāti by Devayānī, Yadu was born, the eldest son; and in the lineage of Yadu there arose one famed as Devamīḍha.

sanskrit: yādavas tasya ca sutaḥ śūras trailokyasaṃmataḥ śūrasya śaurir nṛvaro vasudevo mahāyaśāḥ
english: His son was the Yādava Śūra, honored throughout the three worlds; and of Śūra came his son, the foremost of men, the far-famed Vasudeva.

sanskrit: dhanuṣy anavaraḥ śūraḥ kārtavīryasamo yudhi tadvīryaś cāpi tatraiva kule śinir abhūn nṛpaḥ
english: Unsurpassed in archery, a brave man equal to Kārtavīrya in battle—and of like prowess, in that very line, was born King Śini.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu devakasya mahātmanaḥ duhituḥ svayaṃvare rājan sarvakṣatrasamāgame
english: Now at that very time, O king, at the self-choice ceremony of the daughter of great-souled Devaka, where all the warrior caste had assembled,

sanskrit: tatra vai devakīṃ devīṃ vasudevārtham āptavān nirjitya pārthivān sarvān ratham āropayac chiniḥ
english: there indeed Śini, vanquishing all the kings, won the lady Devakī for Vasudeva's sake and set her upon his chariot.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā devakīṃ śaure rathasthāṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ nāmṛṣyata mahātejāḥ somadattaḥ śiner nṛpa
english: Seeing that Devakī standing on Śini's chariot, O king, the bull among men, the mighty Somadatta, could not endure it.

sanskrit: tayor yuddham abhūd rājan dinārdhaṃ citram adbhutam bāhuyuddhaṃ subalinoḥ śakraprahrādayor iva
english: A combat arose between the two, O king, wondrous and astonishing, lasting half a day—a wrestling match of two mighty men, like that of Śakra and Prahrāda.

sanskrit: śininā somadattas tu prasahya bhuvi pātitaḥ asim udyamya keśeṣu pragṛhya ca padā hataḥ
english: By Śini, Somadatta was overpowered and flung to the ground; and seizing him by the hair and raising his sword, Śini struck him with his foot.
